julgado.behavior: The handler computes isAttendee by matching the user's email against booking.attendees by email only (line 52). It throws FORBIDDEN only if the user is not a team admin/owner, not the organizer, and not an attendee (lines 54-56). An attendee who passes this check can add guests; the handler then calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (line 165) and sendAddGuestsEmails (line 168) for the new guests.

consequences.consequence: An attendee matched only by email passes the permission check and can add guests to the booking.
The handler updates the calendar event and sends emails/invites to the added guests on the organizer's behalf.
Any attendee can use this to send invites/emails to arbitrary addresses.
The attendee's email is not verified/confirmed, so identity is established by email match alone.

julgado.remainingDefect: Any person listed as an attendee (matched solely by email, with no confirmation of the email) can add arbitrary guest addresses to a booking, causing calendar updates and invite emails to be sent to those addresses under the organizer's event. Trigger: an authenticated user whose email equals an attendee's email calls the add-guests handler with arbitrary guest emails. Whether attendees should be allowed at all, or whether email confirmation is required, is a design question the checker did not find to be a factual error.

julgado.behavior: At MultiEmail.tsx line 46, the Tooltip is rendered with the hard-coded English string content="Remove email". consequences.consequence: The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded English and bypasses the translation mechanism.
The component already calls useLocale (t) and the neighbouring label uses t("add_another"), so t is available for this string.
Users with a non-English locale see the tooltip in English instead of their language.

julgado.remainingDefect: The remove-button tooltip always displays the English text "Remove email" regardless of the user's selected locale, because it is not wrapped in t(...) and has no locale key. It is triggered whenever the tooltip is shown for a user with a non-English locale. This is a localization inconsistency only; nothing crashes, returns a wrong result, loses data or breaks a caller.

julgado.behavior: The code builds `message` as a template string `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always a non-empty string, then passes `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` to showToast as an error toast. The `||` fallback can never be used. If `err.data?.code` is undefined, the toast text begins with "undefined: ".

consequences.consequence: The template string is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code.
When err.data?.code is undefined, the user sees an error toast reading "undefined: ...".
The user can see an untranslated raw message in the toast.

julgado.remainingDefect: When an error arrives without `err.data?.code` (e.g. a non-TRPC or network error), the error toast shows "undefined: <message>" instead of the intended translated fallback "unable_to_add_guests", because the template string is always truthy and the fallback never runs. The untranslated-raw-message claim is not verified by the notes. The impact is a confusing error toast text only; nothing crashes, and no data is lost or corrupted.

julgado.behavior: The update action in app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb (lines 9-11) only calls render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...). julgado.behavior: Line 11 of embed.html.erb outputs request.referer with ERB's `<%= %>`, which HTML-escapes the value (a single quote becomes '). The referer is not marked html_safe, so it is emitted escaped inside the inline script string.

julgado.behavior: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 calls Kernel#open(url) and passes the result's .read to Readability::Document.new, with no scheme validation. Callers lib/topic_retriever.rb:52 and lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 pass the URL through. invalid_host? at lib/topic_retriever.rb:14-19 checks only the host, not the scheme.

consequences.consequence: The URL scheme is never validated before Kernel#open is called on it.
The URL originates from the embed_url request parameter and RSS item links and is passed through to open without scheme checks.
With open-uri, Kernel#open can execute commands for strings beginning with '|' or read local files, so attacker-controlled input could lead to command execution or local file disclosure.
The host check in TopicRetriever may limit exploitability, but the notes say this does not contradict the comment.

julgado.remainingDefect: Kernel#open is called on an externally influenced URL with no scheme validation. Input such as a string starting with '|' or a local file path, supplied via embed_url or an RSS item link, can reach open. Because open-uri's Kernel#open treats those as commands or file paths, this could allow command execution or local file reads. The host-only check in invalid_host? may reduce but does not eliminate the exposure, since the notes do not show it blocks such strings.

julgado.behavior: topic_embed.rb saves imported feed/remote-page content as a post with cook_method raw_html. consequences.consequence: Imported HTML skips the sanitizer because cook_method is raw_html and cooking returns the raw content

The url is interpolated unescaped into an href attribute, allowing attribute injection or a malicious URL

julgado.behavior: At app/models/topic_embed.rb:13, `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends the footer in place onto the `contents` string passed as the argument to `self.import(user, url, title, contents)`. This mutates the caller's string object rather than creating a new one.

Mutates the caller's string in place, a side effect visible to the caller.

julgado.remainingDefect: Calling import with a frozen string for contents raises FrozenError, and calling import twice with the same string object duplicates the footer in the content (and the caller's original string is altered). Triggered by frozen string input or by reusing the same string object across imports.

julgado.behavior: At embed.js:17 the message handler does `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. It ignores the message only when e.origin is not a substring of the discourseUrl string. So an empty origin, or any origin that is a substring of the URL (e.g. a prefix or partial host), passes the check rather than being rejected by exact comparison.

consequences.consequence: The check is a substring test rather than an exact origin comparison, so an empty origin or any origin appearing inside the discourseUrl string passes the filter.
Messages from origins other than the Discourse origin can be accepted by the handler (weakened origin validation).
A concrete exploit or specific damage resulting from accepting such messages (e.g. what the handler does with the message data).

julgado.remainingDefect: The origin validation is too loose: a message event whose e.origin is an empty string or a substring of discourseUrl (for example 'https://disc' or a bare host fragment if it appears in the URL) is processed as if it came from the Discourse site, instead of being rejected. Exact equality with the URL's origin would be needed.

julgado.behavior: Line 13 builds the post body by interpolating the url directly into `#{url}` with no HTML escaping. Line 11 only checks that the url matches /^https?:\/\//, which does not restrict quotes or markup. Line 22 creates the post with cook_method raw_html, and post.rb:133 returns raw content without sanitizing for that cook method. The Nokogiri pass in absolutize_urls does not strip markup, so the url ends up in the output as written.

consequences.consequence: A url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML, because it is unescaped, the post is cooked as raw_html, and no sanitization is applied.
The injected markup is rendered through `raw post.cooked`, which allows attribute breakout or script injection (XSS) for viewers of the topic.
Escaping with ERB::Util.html_escape or CGI.escapeHTML for both the href and the link text would fix the problem.

julgado.remainingDefect: A url that starts with http:// or https:// but contains a single quote, angle brackets or other markup (for example `http://x/' onmouseover='...` or `http://x/<script>...`) is inserted unescaped into the raw_html post body. julgado.behavior: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, MaybeSupported is set to `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported` and does not consider an undefined rule (the skipToken case). julgado.behavior: At useAbilities.ts:301-302 a comment says 'All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition' above `const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);`.
